## Trial `etcd-member-replacement-ubuntu16__7iTzfqK`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built the required 3-member etcd cluster with application keys, directly demonstrated node3's permanent loss with quorum-preserved service on node1/node2, replaced the lost member on node3 via a clean etcdctl remove/add + existing-cluster join, and verified restoration to 3 healthy members with all original keys (plus the interim write) intact from both node1 and the rebuilt node3. All four material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with matching boot-identity changes and post-reboot recovery, cross-checked consistently against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is high: the only non-trivial mutation outside the direct task path (an initial mis-bootstrapped standalone start on all three nodes caused by apt/config-ordering) was fully diagnosed and reverted before the final cluster was built, with no residue in the after-executor snapshots.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.950 | 57/4 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **baseline-cluster — Satisfied:** Run a three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
  - **Why:** After resolving an initial apt-triggered standalone-bootstrap misconfiguration (stop/wipe/disable then re-enable/start together), cluster-health and member list show all 3 members healthy (cmd-04227ea3c0664f07). Application keys (/app/config/db_host, /app/config/feature_flag, /app/service/name, /app/counter) were written on node1 (cmd-78d1fc3ecd3b43dd) and read back successfully on node2 and node3 (cmd-4eab99c40c80442b, cmd-9c9b22413db9496a).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-04227ea3c0664f07`, `cmd-78d1fc3ecd3b43dd`, `cmd-4eab99c40c80442b`, `cmd-9c9b22413db9496a`
- **node3-loss-quorum-preserved — Satisfied:** node3 member is permanently lost; cluster continues functioning during the disruption
  - **Why:** etcd was stopped and its data directory wiped on node3 (cmd-8c6cd05357a8409e), simulating unrecoverable loss. cluster-health from node1 immediately afterward shows node3 unreachable while node1 and node2 remain healthy, and a new write (/app/counter -> 43) succeeded, directly demonstrating quorum-preserved service during the bounded disruption (cmd-864afd91b2b9453b).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8c6cd05357a8409e`, `cmd-864afd91b2b9453b`
- **replace-member — Satisfied:** Replace the lost node3 member with a working member on the same system (node3)
  - **Why:** The dead member (70295956b9250d21) was removed via etcdctl (cmd-70ab0b87c8f34cda), a new member was added for node3 (ID 4edf739d42c7d079, cmd-93b8a551a9834182), node3's config was updated with the returned ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER and ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER_STATE=existing (cmd-afec736ba7b64ae8), and etcd was started on node3, with logs showing it joined the existing cluster, elected the standing leader, and published successfully (cmd-b03fb08821a44b5c).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-70ab0b87c8f34cda`, `cmd-93b8a551a9834182`, `cmd-afec736ba7b64ae8`, `cmd-b03fb08821a44b5c`
- **cluster-restored-keys-intact — Satisfied:** Cluster is restored to three healthy members with the existing keys intact
  - **Why:** Post-replacement, cluster-health and member list from node1 show 3/3 healthy members (node1, node2, new node3), and all original application keys plus the new counter value (43) are readable from node1 (cmd-a4fc73ea236f4c0f) and independently confirmed readable on the rebuilt node3 itself (cmd-6c5766bc1b854cb2).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a4fc73ea236f4c0f`, `cmd-6c5766bc1b854cb2`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. All state-changing commands trace to a task purpose: package installation, cluster configuration, the required loss simulation, member remove/add, and the mandatory restart protocol. The one deviation from a straight path was that the first `systemctl start etcd` on all three nodes (cmd-16b3e05c6e464dad, cmd-0abc064390d94480, cmd-13cd76c3fae04368) bootstrapped each node as its own standalone single-member cluster (apt-installed default config took effect before the appended config was fully honored on start, and node2 additionally failed to start). The executor correctly diagnosed this, then fully reverted it via a bounded stop/wipe/disable sequence on all three nodes (cmd-032f2f52e3194920, cmd-5d0eb45762524555, cmd-8a369837921c4934) before cleanly re-enabling and restarting together (cmd-874fe9beb61643ee, cmd-a9616de5e38d4d75, cmd-8ce71e781468417c) to form the correct 3-member cluster. This was a low-risk, fully-restored corrective action directly serving the baseline-cluster prerequisite, not an abandoned experiment. No residue, no failed/conflicting services, no unnecessary exposure, and no unrelated mutations were observed; post-executor lifecycle snapshots show only expected boot-identity and transient systemd-private temp-file churn from the required reboots, with no failed-services or package-health issues on any node.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-16b3e05c6e464dad`, `cmd-0abc064390d94480`, `cmd-13cd76c3fae04368`, `cmd-032f2f52e3194920`, `cmd-5d0eb45762524555`, `cmd-8a369837921c4934`, `cmd-874fe9beb61643ee`, `cmd-a9616de5e38d4d75`, `cmd-8ce71e781468417c`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node3:package-health`
